subject.declared_domain: the ratified term registry for the system ontology -- the file three wave-1 D-rail cards cite via resolves_via as the home of their definitions

methodology.evidence: Read at HEAD: version 3.25, top-level keys {version, changelog, terms}, terms is a dict of 67 entries and changelog a list of 39. Hand-authored and git-reviewed -- it COMPOSES nothing mechanically and INVENTS the term vocabulary itself.
methodology.how: A hand-authored YAML registry of ratified terms. Each entry declares a term and points at its home via resolves_via; the wave-1 D1/D2/D3 cards cite line ranges in it as REGISTRY ENTRIES that declare but do not duplicate.

invents.note: the term vocabulary and its resolves_via convention

declared_opinions: which terms are ratified at all -- membership is an editorial act, not a derivation, so the registry's coverage is its authors' opinion

cadence.evidence: No declared rhythm: this is a git-reviewed file changed by commit, not by a scheduled producer. Last change measured at 2026-08-24T14:24:49-04:00 @07391cdc54, 2 days before carding. live_matches_declared is not_applicable because no rhythm is declared to match.

persistence.evidence: 120,027 bytes on disk, git-TRACKED (`git log -1` resolves @07391cdc54). Editable by commit and reviewed in git, which is the authority the file's own ruling claims.

co_resident_stores.note: wave-1 D1/D2/D3 cite three line ranges :461-466, :467-472, :473-478 in THIS ONE FILE: three registry entries, one artifact

coverage.evidence: COUNTED from the parsed file: 67 terms, 39 changelog entries. ⛔ THE DENOMINATOR THAT MATTERS IS NOT COUNTABLE FROM THIS FILE: 67 of WHAT? The universe is 'terms this estate uses', which has no enumerable population, so a completeness ratio cannot be formed. Recording the countable numerator with the uncountable denominator named rather than inventing a ratio.
coverage.universe: ratified terms of the system ontology
coverage.denominator: 67 terms registered; the population of terms IN USE across the estate is not enumerable, so no coverage ratio is computable
explicitly_out: terms used in the estate but never submitted for ratification -- unbounded and unmeasurable from this artifact

key.evidence: Keys are term names in a flat dict under `terms`. Stable across versions by convention (the changelog records additions rather than renames), but I did NOT diff historical versions to prove no term was ever renamed -- so stability is INFERRED while the id space itself is MEASURED.
key.key_expression: a member is an entry of the $.terms MAPPING; key = the term name (the mapping key)

failure_mode.evidence: EXERCISED: a lookup for a term that cannot exist. Parsed the file and queried terms['zzz_not_a_term'] -- raises KeyError, i.e. a LOUD absence rather than a silent default. POSITIVE CONTROL: a term that does exist returns its entry in the same run, so the arms are reachable from different truths. A consumer that wraps the lookup in a bare except would convert that loud KeyError into a silent miss, which is a CONSUMER hazard and not a property of this store.
failure_mode.returns_on_failure: KeyError on a missing term -- loud
silent_degrade_paths: a consumer catching the KeyError broadly would erase the signal

verdict.why: A hand-authored, git-reviewed, owned registry with a loud failure mode -- the strongest trust profile of the nine stores this lane carded. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on one axis only: its coverage denominator is structurally uncomputable, so nothing can say whether 67 terms is most of the vocabulary or a fraction of it. That is a property of the domain, not a defect in the artifact.
